entries.title: Blank protected live results on membership revocation
entries.competitorOutcome: InstantDB and SpacetimeDB directly evicted protected rows from already-subscribed clients when membership was removed.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: LLP 0053's obligation, terminal proof, acknowledgement, lease, and no-future-delivery contract.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A declaration-bound delete or downgrade generically wakes the protected live query, denies its rerun, terminally deletes its visible and retained state, and fences later delivery.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Resource-scoped and app-scoped sessions-mode tests cover delete and downgrade, blank-before-return, fresh denial, no later delivery, exact acknowledgement, and no fixture-specific invalidation; frozen TODO-12 and CHAT-13 rerun PASS.

entries.title: Make live disposal idempotent across authority retirement
entries.competitorOutcome: Mainstream client lifecycles allow ordinary unsubscribe cleanup after logout or listener failure without turning already-complete retirement into an application error.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Unknown foreign subscription identifiers and ownership mismatches must still fail closed.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A handle may dispose repeatedly after its own authority-driven retirement and receives a typed already-retired success, while unowned identifiers remain errors.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Lifecycle tests cover logout then dispose, revocation then dispose, double dispose, supersession, foreign id refusal, and no duplicate server effects; frozen logout scenarios retain PASS without diagnostic noise.

entries.title: Make ephemeral subscription transport readiness unskippable
entries.competitorOutcome: InstantDB room topics/presence and Firebase RTDB listeners establish their transport as part of the ordinary subscription path.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: One connection manager may safely multiplex durable and ephemeral lanes under explicit lifecycle control.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The generated ephemeral subscribe path either establishes and awaits its manager itself or emits an exact actionable readiness diagnostic; the Guide's first example is complete.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A fresh connection label receives its first ephemeral change from the documented/generated one-path recipe without a prior durable live query; codegen preserves specific row types.

entries.title: Retry effect-free authorization reservations below app code
entries.competitorOutcome: Convex, Supabase, and SpacetimeDB settled the frozen two-actor append through their normal transaction calls without an application-authored authorization-reservation loop.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Retries are permitted only when the typed receipt proves no effect committed; ambiguous or committed outcomes remain visible and never replay automatically.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The standard generated client performs a bounded whole-operation retry for effect-free reservation staleness and retains structured attempt evidence.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A two-client barrier test induces one stale reservation, commits two messages exactly once in deterministic order, exposes two attempts in diagnostics, and never retries an ambiguous or effect-committed result.

entries.title: Bring protected retained history and queued writes to the normal client path
entries.competitorOutcome: Firebase and InstantDB made retained data and offline settlement available through ordinary application clients rather than a custom sync engine.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Server authority, lease-bounded protected bytes, explicit settlement, user-switch deletion, and fail-closed replay parity.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: An ordinary generated React query/mutation pair can opt into protected cold retention and a restart-safe outbox with visible cache provenance and settlement.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A cold process renders authorized rows offline, queues a mutation across restart, settles exactly once on reconnect, handles conflict explicitly, and deletes or quarantines protected bytes on expiry/revocation.

entries.title: Make first build use a prepared Ibex runtime
entries.competitorOutcome: SpacetimeDB reached a sub-second module loop and InstantDB reached a hosted temporary target without compiling a runtime toolchain.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: The local target remains the complete real runtime, and source build remains a supported explicit fallback.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Supported machines acquire a verified prepared Hermes/Ibex artifact and reach the first Snapback build without an implicit source compilation.
entries.acceptanceWitness: A clean machine with no sibling Ibex checkout runs bootstrap, verifies artifact identity and launch, and builds the frozen external Todo/Chat apps without compiling Hermes.

entries.title: Expose authority and cache provenance as inspectable evidence
entries.competitorOutcome: Firebase exposed cache/server metadata and rule coverage; Supabase exposed SQL/RLS; InstantDB supplied debugTransact for relationship-policy investigation.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Diagnostics reveal decision structure and provenance without leaking protected data, credentials, or policy secrets.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: A structured inspection path explains the actor, captured authority dependency, admitting/denying gate, transport, cache origin, and settlement state for a query or mutation.
entries.acceptanceWitness: An outsider denial, membership revocation, retained offline read, and concurrent mutation each emit redacted machine-readable explanations that bind to the authoritative receipt.

entries.title: Pave deterministic ordered append and stable cursor reads
entries.competitorOutcome: Every competitor supplied a workable server-authoritative order, but Firebase exposed a hot counter and SpacetimeDB needed a request/result table for cursor pages.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Commit authority and conflict outcomes remain deterministic and target-portable.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: The Guide and generated surface provide one canonical ordered-append/cursor pattern with direct concurrent settlement evidence.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Twenty two-client appends settle without duplicates, ambiguous order, or application hot-counter retry; two cursor pages remain disjoint under a concurrent newer insert.

entries.title: Keep ephemeral state native rather than imitating durable TTL workarounds
entries.competitorOutcome: Convex and SpacetimeDB could emulate typing with durable rows and cleanup glue, but InstantDB demonstrated the better native-room outcome.
entries.snapbackPropertyToPreserve: Typed non-durable room state, TTL, connection identity, and separation from the durable journal.
entries.snapbackNativeOutcome: Improve the existing native ephemeral path rather than adding provider-shaped durable TTL abstractions to satisfy the fixture.
entries.acceptanceWitness: Typing and presence pass with zero durable application rows, native expiry/disconnect evidence, typed generated rows, and one documented subscription lifecycle.
